title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)'. Grothendieck is building an axiomatic framework, an 'Atlas', for a tame ('modérée') topology. It deals with 'figures' F, their 'stations' or lieux X in a class M, the ordered sets F~ of pieces of a figure, 'ombres' (shadows), sups and infs of figures, and 'raffinements' (refinements) of figures. The axioms are numbered At 9, At 9_Σ, At 10, At 11, At 11', At 12. On p.78 he has just stated At 9_Σ, a compatibility or disjointness criterion relative to a class Σ of ordered sets ('Σ-dalles'), together with its corollaries 9'' (Σ = Σ_M) and 9' (Σ = all ordered sets).

This page is pure bookkeeping of logical dependencies among the axioms. It gives three successive diagrams, the middle one crossed out. The final diagram reads:
- At 9_Σ + At 10 ⇒ At 9_Σ and At 12.
- At 9_Σ ⇒ At 9 (criterion of disjunction/compatibility by the lieux).
- At 12 ⇒ At 10 and At 12 ⇒ At 11'.
- At 11 ⇒ At 11'.

He glosses the last two axioms as gluing conditions:
- At 11 ⟺ 'recollement des raffinements' in F = Sup F_i for an arbitrary family.
- At 11' ⟺ the same gluing for I finite.

The top diagram also notes At 12 ⇒ At 11' when F~ is finite. An implication to At 11 itself is crossed out.

The key remark: among these axioms, At 11 is the only one stating an existence criterion for the sup of an INFINITE family of figures. For that reason it cannot follow from At 12, which only involves finite sups. So At 9_Σ + At 10 (equivalently At 9_Σ + At 12) implies every axiom except At 11.

He then proposes to replace At 11 by an equivalent statement modulo At 11'. On the next page this becomes At 11 bis, a filtered-sup condition: an increasing filtered family of refinements of F whose restrictions to each X ∈ F~ have a sup has a global sup. This gives At 11 ⟺ At 11 bis + At 11'.

The outcome (p.80) is the 'reduced' axiom systems {At 9_Σ, At 10, At 11 bis} or {At 9, At 11 bis, At 12}. These separate finite gluing/compatibility conditions from a single filtered-colimit, local-finiteness type existence condition. This is the standard pattern 'finite conditions + filtered colimits = arbitrary colimits', applied to a sheaf-like gluing of refinements.
errors: 'At 11 is not implied by At 12 because it involves an infinite sup' is a heuristic, not a proof of independence; no countermodel is given.

The page states At 12 ⇒ At 11' only 'pour F~ fini' in the top diagram, but unconditionally in the final diagram. There is a slight inconsistency or tacit strengthening; the finite restriction likely matters.

The equivalence At 9_Σ + At 10 ⟺ At 9_Σ + At 12 is asserted without the argument for At 9_Σ + At 12 ⇒ At 10 being nontrivial (it follows from At 12 ⇒ At 10). The converse direction, At 9_Σ + At 10 ⇒ At 12, is not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'Atlas' of figures for a tame topology, with sups/infs of figures, refinements and stations
ideas.modern_name: tame topology / o-minimal-like axiomatics; lattices of definable sets; stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimality, 1980s); Grothendieck's programme in Esquisse §5
ideas.where_published: Programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; the detailed axioms appear unpublished

ideas.what: Gluing ('recollement') of refinements over F = Sup F_i, split into a finite gluing condition (At 11') and a filtered-sup existence condition (At 11 bis)
ideas.modern_name: sheaf condition / decomposition of colimits into finite colimits plus filtered colimits
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard category theory (e.g. Gabriel–Ulmer, SGA4 style arguments)

ideas.what: Separating finitary axioms from the single infinitary one (independence heuristic)
ideas.modern_name: finitary vs infinitary axioms; local finiteness

missed.claim: The page belongs to a detailed, unpublished axiomatization of tame topology ('Atlas' of figures, stations, Σ-dalles, saturation of an atlas). It is a concrete realization of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse, distinct from o-minimality. This page itself only organizes axiom dependencies.
missed.quote: Le seul axiome qui échappe à At 9_Σ + At 10 (équivalemment : At 9_Σ + At 12) est At 11, qui implique un sup infini.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing this axiom system (finite gluing + filtered sups of refinements) with o-minimal structures or with stratified/exit-path frameworks could show whether Grothendieck's tame topology differs substantively. That comparison has not been made in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Interesting as evidence of the unpublished tame-topology axiomatics, but the page itself is routine logical bookkeeping of axiom implications. It has no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Paragraph: 'Dans ces axiomes, le seul qui fait état, dans la notion d'un critère d'existence pour un sup d'une famille infinie de figures, est At 11' ('le seul', 'critère' inserted above a struck word, 'infinie' underlined).
Parenthesis reads '(équivalemment : At 9_Σ + At 12)' rather than 'équivalent'.
Under At 9: probably '(critère de disj. par les lieux)', i.e. disjonction/compatibility, rather than 'dissoc.'.
Top right: 'At 11' ⟺ At 11 pour F = Sup F_i fini' and 'At 12 ⇒ At 11' pour F~ fini' with '⇒ At 11' struck out; the first line is 'At 11 ⟺ At 11 pour F = Sup F_i quelc.'.
The final diagram also has an arrow At 11 ⇒ At 11', and the gloss for At 11' reads 'F = Sup_{i∈I} F_i pour I fini'.
Last line: 'On pourrait alors remplacer At 11 par un énoncé qui soit équivalent, compte tenu de At 11' :'.
The ending of the paragraph '- la seule autre qui fasse intervenir un sup fini est ...' is illegible; the transcription's '𝓘' is doubtful.
